ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, the power supply voltage is \( u = 220\sqrt{2} \sin(628t) \, \text{V} \), and the readings of ammeters \( A_1 \), \( A_2 \), and \( A_3 \) are the same. If the power supply voltage is changed to \( u = 220\sqrt{2} \sin(314t) \, \text{V} \), which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The reading of \( A_1 \) is twice the reading of \( A_3 \)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the AC power supply is connected to the upper and lower two common wires, forming three parallel branches. The left branch is an ammeter A1 connected in series with an inductor L; the middle branch is an ammeter A2 connected in series with a capacitor C; the right branch is an ammeter A3 connected in series with a resistor R. Therefore, the voltages across the two ends of the three branches are the same. Reasoning: The original voltage is u = 220√2 sin(628t) V, the angular frequency is ω1 = 628 rad/s, and the readings of the three ammeters are the same. After the change, u = 220√2 sin(314t) V, the effective value of the voltage is still 220 V, but the angular frequency becomes ω2 = 314 rad/s, that is, half of the original. In the parallel circuit, the effective value of the voltage of each branch remains unchanged. The current in the resistor branch I3 = U/R is unrelated to frequency, so the A3 reading remains unchanged. The inductive reactance of the inductor branch XL = ωL, and when the frequency is halved, XL is also halved, so the current in the inductor branch I1 = U/XL becomes 2 times the original. Since the original readings of A1 and A3 were the same, after changing the frequency, the reading of A1 is 2 times that of A3.
